questions.question: Which condition characterizes an orthogonal matrix Q in R^{n x n}?
questions.choice_A: Q^T Q = I
questions.choice_B: Q Q = I
questions.choice_C: Q^2 = I

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes SO(n) from O(n)?
questions.choice_A: SO(n) contains reflections while O(n) does not
questions.choice_B: SO(n) consists of orthogonal matrices with determinant 1, whereas O(n) allows determinant ±1
questions.choice_C: SO(n) includes non-invertible matrices, O(n) does not
questions.choice_D: SO(n) is not a group, O(n) is

questions.question: What geometric transformations do real orthogonal matrices represent on R^n?
questions.choice_A: Translations and scalings
questions.choice_B: Shears and projections
questions.choice_C: Rotations and reflections (isometries about the origin)

questions.question: Which property is preserved under multiplication by an orthogonal matrix Q on the left, i.e., x -> Qx?
questions.choice_A: Component-wise magnitude
questions.choice_B: Entrywise sparsity pattern
questions.choice_C: L1 norm

questions.question: For an orthogonal matrix Q, which of the following is always true?
questions.choice_A: det(Q) = 0
questions.choice_B: det(Q) = -1
questions.choice_C: All singular values of Q equal 1

questions.question: Which statement about inverses and transposes of orthogonal matrices is correct?
questions.choice_A: Q^{-1} exists if and only if Q is symmetric
questions.choice_B: Q^{-1} = Q only for reflections
questions.choice_C: Q^{-1} = Q^T for any orthogonal Q
questions.choice_D: Q^{-1} = Q^2 for any orthogonal Q

questions.question: What is the dimension of the Lie algebra so(n) associated with SO(n)?
questions.choice_A: n

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes so(n)?
questions.choice_A: The set of symmetric matrices with trace 0
questions.choice_B: The set of skew-symmetric matrices with the commutator bracket
questions.choice_C: The set of all orthogonal matrices with determinant 1
questions.choice_D: The set of upper-triangular matrices with unit diagonal

questions.question: Which property about eigenvalues of a real orthogonal matrix is true?
questions.choice_A: All eigenvalues are real and nonnegative
questions.choice_B: All eigenvalues have modulus less than 1
questions.choice_C: Eigenvalues lie on the unit circle; complex ones come in conjugate pairs

questions.question: What does det(Q) indicate geometrically for Q in O(n)?
questions.choice_A: The amount of scaling along coordinate axes
questions.choice_B: The rotation angle magnitude
questions.choice_C: Whether the transformation is volume increasing

questions.question: Which is a key numerical property of a Householder reflection H = I - 2uu^T with ||u||=1?
questions.choice_A: It is sparse only when u is sparse
questions.choice_B: It requires O(n^2) flops to apply to a vector
questions.choice_C: It can zero out all but one component of a vector in O(n) time
questions.choice_D: It is not orthogonal unless u is an eigenvector

questions.question: Givens rotations are particularly useful because they:
questions.choice_A: Simultaneously zero out multiple components in one step
questions.choice_B: Operate on only two coordinates at a time, enabling targeted elimination with local updates
questions.choice_C: Are projections onto coordinate axes
questions.choice_D: Change vector norms in a controlled way

questions.question: Which statement about the singular values of QW, where Q is orthogonal and W is any real matrix, is correct?
questions.choice_A: They are the squares of the singular values of W
questions.choice_B: They are unchanged from those of W
questions.choice_C: They equal the eigenvalues of W

questions.question: Which of the following gives a local parameterization of SO(n) near the identity?
questions.choice_A: Q = \/ A, where A is any matrix
questions.choice_B: Q = \/(I + A), where A is symmetric
questions.choice_C: Q = \exp(S), with S skew-symmetric

questions.question: What is a defining property of the Cayley transform applied to a real skew-symmetric matrix S?
questions.choice_A: Q = (I - S)(I + S)^{-1} is orthogonal and can represent any element of O(n)
questions.choice_B: Q = (I - S)(I + S)^{-1} is orthogonal provided (I + S) is invertible, but it cannot produce orthogonal matrices with eigenvalue −1
questions.choice_C: Q is symmetric for any S
questions.choice_D: Q always lies in SO(n) and includes reflections

questions.question: Which limitation applies to the Cayley transform as a parameterization of O(n)?
questions.choice_A: It only covers matrices with determinant −1
questions.choice_B: It fails for any n > 2
questions.choice_C: It excludes orthogonal matrices with eigenvalue −1 and is not surjective onto O(n)
questions.choice_D: It does not preserve inner products

questions.question: What can be said about det(\exp(S)) for a real skew-symmetric matrix S?
questions.choice_A: It equals 0
questions.choice_B: It equals −1
questions.choice_C: It equals 1, so \exp(S) \in SO(n)
questions.choice_D: It depends on \operatorname{trace}(S) in a nontrivial way

questions.question: Which statement accurately contrasts Givens rotations and Householder reflections in practice?
questions.choice_A: Givens are global transformations; Householders are strictly local
questions.choice_B: Givens are preferred for streaming/sparse updates; Householders are preferred for dense, batched elimination
questions.choice_C: Householders cannot be composed to form general orthogonal matrices
questions.choice_D: Givens do not preserve norms, Householders do

questions.question: Which property does left-multiplication by an orthogonal matrix Q impart to a weight matrix W in a neural network?
questions.choice_A: It changes the Frobenius norm ||W||_F
questions.choice_B: It alters the singular values of W, affecting its spectral norm
questions.choice_C: It preserves 2-norm conditioning and the distribution of singular values, acting as an isometry on the row space

questions.question: Which structural statement about O(n) is correct?
questions.choice_A: O(n) is connected for all n
questions.choice_B: O(n) has two connected components distinguished by determinant sign; SO(n) is the identity component for n ≥ 2
questions.choice_C: SO(n) has two connected components

questions.question: Which best describes the spectral structure of a real orthogonal matrix Q in terms of real canonical blocks?
questions.choice_A: It is always diagonalizable over R with ±1 on the diagonal
questions.choice_B: It is similar over R to a block-diagonal matrix with 1x1 blocks {+1 or −1} and 2x2 rotation blocks of the form [[\cos\theta, −\sin\theta],[\sin\theta, \cos\theta]]
questions.choice_C: It is always a single Jordan block
